newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-GERMANY'S TOP SIX BATTLE FOR CASH JACKPOT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GERMANY'S TOP SIX BATTLE FOR CASH JACKPOT.

text.p: German soccer kicks off on Friday with a lucrative new six-team tournament that gives champions Bayern Munich and European Cup winners Borussia Dortmund a chance to test their new line-ups.
The tournament, which involves the first six of last year's Bundesliga, will guarantee the participating teams a minimum prize money of 500,000 marks ($277,000).
The winner of the final on July 26 in Leverkusen will have won 2.5 million marks ($1.8 million) even before the actual start of the German league on August 2.
The new event, called Ligapokal (League Cup) replaces the traditional Super Cup curtain raiser which was the equivalent of the English Charity Shield with the champions facing the Cup winners.
Last season's runners-up Bayer Leverkusen play sixth-placed Karlsruhe in the first game on Friday in Aue.
The winner will go on to meet Stuttgart, who came fourth in the league and won the domestic Cup, in the first semifinal in Osnabrueck on July 22.
Borussia Dortmund, who ended up third in the league, play Vfl Bochum, who came fifth, on Sunday in Koblenz. The winner of that match will meet Bayern in the second semifinal in Augsburg on July 23.

Bayern look impressive on paper with Brazilian striker Giovane Elber, who signed from Stuttgart for a 12.5 million marks ($6.9 million) fee, and French international defender Bixente Lizarazu reinforcing last season's star-studded team.
Dortmund, meanwhile, have made no major signing and have kept most of the players who helped them win the European Cup. But they have a new coach in Italian Nevio Scala.
